title: Staff
summary: Who works here, their PINs, phones and pay. The screen has four tabs (People, The schedule, The hours, Shop's clock); this entry covers the top of the screen and the People tab.

who.can: everything on the screen: add people, their details, PINs, pay, phones, last days; the schedule; correct hours; make and remove clock screens
the same as the owner
add people, change their details, set PINs, link phones, set last days, make the schedule, correct and add hours; see the clock screens
who.cannot: see or set pay (no pay badges, no Pay tab, no labour cost in the schedule check); make or remove a clock screen

who.can: see everyone and their pay; set pay (Pay tab); see the schedule with its labour cost, and the hours
who.cannot: add people, change details, PINs, phones or last days; change the schedule; correct hours; the Shop's clock tab is not shown

who.can: read everything on People, The schedule and The hours, pay included
who.cannot: change anything; the Shop's clock tab is not shown

who.can: nothing here: opening /staff sends them to their own start screen
who.cannot: open the screen

get_there: Menu → Operations → Staff. Also: Payroll → “Staff, the schedule and the hours →”; links to /staff#people, /staff#schedule, /staff#attendance, /staff#shop-clock open that tab; /staff#add-person opens the Add people form (Getting set up uses it).
before: At least one active place (branch or central kitchen) for “Where they work”. Warehouses are not offered.
To give someone a login, they must first be added as a member on Settings → People and roles; then their login can be chosen here.

parts.name: Heading and intro
parts.shows: “Staff” and the short text: “Who works here, the schedule, and the hours. Each person clocks in and out on their own phone, by scanning the shop's code, or at the till with their name and PIN. Lateness, leaving early, absence and overtime are shown here, and deducted from pay only when a manager says so on Payroll.”

controls.label: How this works
controls.does: Opens the longer explanation of the screen.

parts.name: In now
parts.shows: Everyone clocked in at this moment, each as a green badge “{name} · since {time}” (month-day and time on the café's clock). Empty: “Nobody is clocked in.” Shown above the tabs, on every tab.

parts.name: Tabs
parts.shows: People, The schedule, The hours, and Shop's clock (only for those who manage staff or settings). Only one shows at a time; what you typed in one tab is kept while you look at another.

controls.label: People / The schedule / The hours / Shop's clock
controls.does: Shows that tab and puts its name in the address (#people, #schedule, #attendance, #shop-clock), so a reload or a shared link opens the same tab.

controls.label: Left / Right arrow, Home, End
controls.does: With a tab focused: move to the next or previous tab (reversed in Arabic and Kurdish), the first or the last.

parts.name: People tab: tools
parts.shows: A search box (6 or more people), Download CSV, and Add people.

controls.label: Find someone…
controls.does: Filters the list as you type. Matches the name, what they do, the phone or the place.
controls.rules: Shown only when there are 6 or more people. Not case-sensitive.

controls.label: Download CSV
controls.does: Downloads staff_YYYY-MM-DD.csv: a row a person with Name, What they do, Phone, Where they work, Started on, Their last day, Works here now (Yes/No), Login, PIN (Set / None yet), In now. Headings are in your language.
controls.rules: Shown when there is at least one person. Pay columns (How they are paid, Pay (IQD), A day's hours, Overtime %, Advances owed (IQD)) only for those who see payroll and only when someone's pay is visible. Phone linked (Yes/No) only for those who manage staff. Amounts are plain numbers.
controls.after: Nothing changes; it is a copy of the list.

controls.label: Add people
controls.does: Opens the “People to add” form in place of the button.

parts.name: People to add (the Add people form)
parts.shows: “A row for each person. A PIN can be set now, or later on their row: let each person type their own. Rows left empty are not added.” A table that starts with 3 empty rows. A row with a problem is marked and says why under the name, with a warning icon.

controls.label: Name
controls.does: Their name.
controls.rules: Required in a row you use. Up to 80 letters. Must not be the same as someone already on the staff.

controls.label: What they do
controls.does: Their job, e.g. Barista.
controls.rules: Optional, up to 60 letters.

controls.label: Phone
controls.does: Their phone number.
controls.rules: Optional, up to 40 characters.

controls.label: Where they work
controls.does: The place they belong to: the café's active branches and central kitchens.
controls.rules: Default: the first place.

controls.label: Started on
controls.does: Their first day (a date).
controls.rules: Default: today. At most a year ahead.

controls.label: Their login, if they have one
controls.does: Links the person to a member's login (“No login” by default).
controls.rules: A login can belong to one person only; choosing the same login on two rows marks both rows.

controls.label: PIN (optional)
controls.does: Their clock-in PIN, typed by them. Only digits are kept (Arabic digits become 0–9).
controls.rules: 4 to 8 digits, not one digit repeated (1111) and not a run (1234, 9876).

controls.label: Remove this row
controls.does: The ✕ at the end of a row: removes it. Removing the last row leaves one empty row.

controls.label: Another row
controls.does: Adds an empty row.

controls.label: Cancel
controls.does: Closes the form; nothing is added.

controls.label: Add to the staff / Add {n} to the staff
controls.does: Adds each ready row one after another (“Adding {done} of {of}…” while it works), then sets its PIN if one was typed. When all are added, the form closes and says “{n} added to the staff.” under the list. Rows that failed stay in the form with the reason; rows added leave it.
controls.rules: Disabled until at least one row is filled and every filled row is free of problems. A row with only its place and date (filled in for you) counts as empty and is skipped.
controls.after: Each person is added to the staff list, the till's clock list (if they work at that branch) and the schedule. The audit trail records it. A PIN that could not be set does not stop the person being added: set it later on their PIN tab.

parts.name: The list of people
parts.shows: One line a person: initials in a circle (green when clocked in), name, what they do · place, and badges: “In since {time}”, “Last day {day}” (yellow while still to come, grey once passed), “Starts later” (start date in the future), “PIN set” or “No PIN yet”, “Phone linked”, and for those who see payroll the pay (“{amount} a month” / “{amount} a day” / “{amount} an hour”) or “Pay not set”. People who no longer work here are shown greyed.

controls.label: {name}: open
controls.does: The whole line: opens that person's panel beside the list.

controls.label: Payroll and advances →
controls.does: Opens Payroll.

parts.name: A person's panel
parts.shows: Their initials, name, what they do (or “No job written yet”) and “In since {time}”. Facts: Where, Started, Phone, Login, PIN (Set / None yet), Their phone (Phone linked / Not linked; for those who manage staff), Pay (with “{hours} hours a day” and “overtime at {percent}%”, or “Not set”) and Advances owed (for those who see payroll). Below, a tab for each thing to change.

controls.label: Close
controls.does: The ✕: closes the panel. Escape or a tap outside it also closes it; focus goes back to the person's line.

controls.label: Details
controls.does: The person's form: Name, What they do, Phone, Where they work, Started on, Their login, if they have one; “Save” and “Cancel”.
controls.rules: Save is disabled without a name or a place. Started on cannot be after their last day, nor after hours already recorded for them.
controls.after: The list, the till's clock and the schedule show the new details. Recorded in the audit trail.

controls.label: Set a PIN / New PIN
controls.does: “Let {name} type it: 4 to 8 digits, not one digit over and over, nor a run like 1234. They clock in and out at the till with their name and this PIN.” Two boxes (PIN, The same PIN again) and “Save the PIN”.
controls.rules: Save the PIN is disabled until the first box has 4 characters. The two must match.
controls.after: They clock in at the till with this PIN from now on. A new PIN also lifts the pause after too many wrong PINs that day. The panel closes after a moment.

controls.label: Pay
controls.does: How they are paid (By the month / By the day / By the hour), the rate (its label follows the choice: “Pay a month”, “Pay a day”, “Pay an hour”), A day's hours (default 8), Overtime at (% of an hour's pay; empty: the café's rule), Why it changes (optional); “Save the pay” and “Cancel”. Note: “Overtime is each hour worked beyond a day's hours. An hour's pay is an hourly rate; a day's pay over a day's hours; or a month's pay over 30 days and a day's hours.”
controls.rules: Rate is required and above 0. A day's hours: more than 0 and at most 16. Overtime: 100% to 300%; empty uses the café's rule (150% unless changed).
controls.after: Used by the next payroll draft. A draft made before the change shows that it is out of date and must be drafted again. The schedule check's labour cost uses it at once. Recorded with its reason in the audit trail.

controls.label: Their phone
controls.does: Links the person's own phone so it clocks them in and out (see the steps under “Their phone” below).
controls.who: staff.manage, and only for someone who works here now

controls.label: Last day / Works here again
controls.does: For someone working: “After their last day they no longer clock in, and their hours on the schedule after it are taken off. Their records and pay stay.” A date (default today), Why (e.g. moved to Erbil) and “Save their last day”. For someone who has left: Why (e.g. came back after the summer) and “They work here again”.
controls.rules: Why is required (the button stays disabled without it). The last day cannot be before they started; they must be clocked out; no hours may be recorded after it.
controls.after: Their schedule after the last day is deleted. After it they cannot clock in, be put on the schedule or be given an advance. Their records, payrolls and advances stay. Recorded in the audit trail.

parts.name: Their phone (tab in the panel)
parts.shows: With no phone linked, a square to scan is shown at once: “{name}: scan this with your own phone's camera”, steps “Open the camera on your phone and point it at the square.” and “Open the link it shows, and press Link this phone.”, “The square works once, until {time}.” and “Waiting for the phone…”. With a phone linked: “Their phone is linked since {when}.” and “Last used {when}.”

controls.label: The link, to send to their phone
controls.does: The same link as the square, as text (selected when tapped), to send by message if the camera cannot scan.

controls.label: Make a new one
controls.does: Shown when the square is too old (“This square is too old.”): makes a new square and link, good for 10 minutes.

controls.label: Link a new phone
controls.does: With a phone linked: shows a new square, to link a different phone. When the new phone links, the old one stops.

controls.label: Unlink…
controls.does: Shows a Why box (e.g. They lost it) with “Unlink the phone” and “Cancel”.
controls.after: The phone no longer clocks them in. With a clock screen in use, they then clock in on it with their PIN.

controls.label: Close
controls.does: Closes the panel.

controls.label: Done
controls.does: Shown after “Linked: {name}'s phone clocks them in and out now.”: closes the panel.

In now says “Nobody is clocked in.”
“Nobody by that name.” in the list.
No Add people button; the panel shows the facts and, for the accountant, only the Pay tab.

messages.text: Your previous submission may already have been saved. Checking…
messages.when: The connection dropped while saving, and the screen is sending the same save again (up to three more tries, 1, 2 and 4 seconds apart).
messages.do: Wait. It will not be recorded twice.

messages.text: Still no answer. It may have been saved: press the same button again to check. It will not be recorded twice.
messages.when: Three more tries got no answer from the database.
messages.do: Check the connection, then press the same button again. The database recognises the same save and does not record it twice.

messages.text: This retry does not match what was first sent: reload the page and check before doing it again
messages.when: A save was sent again with its first key but different values (for example, the form was changed while it was retrying).
messages.do: Reload the page, check whether the first save went through, then do it again if needed.

messages.text: This was sent by someone else
messages.when: Rare: the same save key was already used by another person's login.
messages.do: Reload the page and do it again.

messages.text: You do not have permission to do this (needs {1})
messages.when: Your roles do not hold the permission named (here usually staff.manage or payroll.run). The database checks every save again, even if a button was shown.
messages.do: Ask the owner to change your roles on Settings → People and roles, or ask someone who may do it.

messages.text: Finish signing in: type the code from your authenticator app
messages.when: Two-step sign-in is on for you and this session has not taken the second step.
messages.do: Reload the page: you are taken to the code step. Type the six digits from your authenticator app.

messages.text: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
messages.when: The sign-in expired or was ended on this device.
messages.do: Sign in again; what you typed may need typing again.

messages.text: The database did not answer, so this may have been saved. Check before trying again.
messages.when: The connection to the database failed during a save that has no automatic retry.
messages.do: Reload the page and look whether the change is there before doing it again.

messages.text: The database is missing an update this screen needs (a migration has not been applied yet).
messages.when: The café's database has not had the update that this part of the screen uses.
messages.do: Tell whoever looks after the system; nothing was saved.

what_if.case: A new barista starts tomorrow
what_if.do: Add people → fill a row with their name, job, place, tomorrow's date; let them type a PIN or set it later. They show “Starts later” until then.

what_if.case: Someone forgot their PIN
what_if.do: Open their line → New PIN, and let them type a new one twice. It also lifts the pause after too many wrong PINs.

what_if.case: Someone lost their phone
what_if.do: Open their line → Their phone → Unlink… with why. Then link the new phone with Link a new phone. Meanwhile they clock in with their PIN.

what_if.case: Someone leaves at the end of the month
what_if.do: Open their line → Last day, choose the date, write why, Save their last day. Make sure they are clocked out. Their last payroll still includes them.

what_if.case: Someone who left comes back
what_if.do: Open their line → Works here again, write why, They work here again. Then put them on the schedule again.

what_if.case: Two people have the same name
what_if.do: Add a surname or a nickname; the screen refuses two identical names.

tips: Let each person type their own PIN; do not choose it for them.
The CSV opens in Excel or Google Sheets; amounts are plain numbers you can add up.
Add several people at once with Another row; empty rows are skipped.

title: Staff → The schedule
summary: Who works when at a place, a week (Saturday to Friday) at a time, typed as 08:00-16:00; and a check of the week against how busy each part of the day usually is, with what the hours cost.

who.can: type and save the week, copy last week, see the check with labour cost
type and save the week, copy last week, see the check of people needed
who.cannot: see the labour cost row and line (no payroll.view)

who.can: see the week (read-only) and the check with labour cost
who.cannot: change the hours

before: People on the staff, with “Where they work” set.
For the check: four weeks of sales with people clocked in. For the labour cost: pay set on Staff; the target on Settings → Rules.

parts.name: Week and place
parts.shows: The week's first and last day (Saturday — Friday) between the arrows; the café's places as chips when there is more than one (the chosen one is green).

controls.label: The week before
controls.does: Shows the week before, at the same place.

controls.label: The week after
controls.does: Shows the next week, at the same place. This is how you make next week's schedule.

controls.label: (a place's name)
controls.does: Shows that place's week. It also makes that place this device's place on every screen.

parts.name: The week's grid
parts.shows: A row for each person of this place (or with hours here this week), with what they do; a column for each day (Saturday … Friday, with month-day). A cell shows: a box for the hours; “—” on a day they do not work here yet or any more; “{place}: 08:00-16:00” in grey when they work at another place that day; the hours as text when you cannot change them or the day's pay is approved.

controls.label: {name}'s hours on {day}
controls.does: Type the hours, e.g. 08:00-16:00. 8-16, 0800-1600 and Arabic digits work too. Empty: not working that day.
controls.rules: One stretch a person a day. Hours that end at or before they start end the next day (18:00-02:00). Start and end cannot be the same. A day whose month's pay is approved cannot change.

controls.label: Save the week
controls.does: Saves all the hours of this place for the week shown, replacing what was saved before.
controls.rules: Disabled until something changed. Each cell must be hours or empty.
controls.after: The till's clock list shows each person's shift today; lateness, leaving early and absence on The hours, Payroll and Reports are measured against it. An Undo button shows for 10 seconds. Recorded in the audit trail.

controls.label: The same hours as the week before
controls.does: Fills the boxes with last week's hours at this place, a week later. Does not save: check, change, then Save the week.
controls.rules: Shown only when last week had hours here. Skips days a person does not work and days whose pay is approved. Overwrites boxes already typed for those days.

controls.label: Undo ({n})
controls.does: For 10 seconds after saving: puts back the week as it was before the save.
controls.after: “Undone: as it was before.”

parts.name: Is the week staffed for how busy it usually is?
parts.shows: Changes as you type, before saving. “From the four weeks to yesterday: what each part of the day usually brings on its weekday, and the {n} orders a person usually serves in an hour. Each cell: the people scheduled at a time, and about how many its orders need.” Rows Morning (5:00–12:00), Afternoon (12:00–17:00), Evening (17:00 to 5:00 the next morning); a cell “{people} · needs {need}” with a mark: ▲ too few, ▽ more than needed, ● nobody when orders usually come, ✓ fine, — no hours and no orders. A Labour row (% of what that day usually sells), for those who see pay. Under it, sentences listing the parts too few, with nobody, or with more than needed; and the week's cost.

parts.name: The lines
parts.shows: A row a person: Who (and job); Pay (“{amount} a month” etc., or red “Pay not set”; “{days} of {all} days here” for a monthly person who joined or left in the month); Worked (“{days} days, {hours}”, with “Overtime {time}”, “Late {n} times”, “Absent {n} days”, red “Still clocked in”); Base; Overtime; Added (with its note and “Tips +{amount}”); Deducted (with note); Advance taken back (“of {owed} owed” when not all); To be paid; Paid. A Total row. Under it: “The pay (gross) is the base and the overtime, with what was added and less what was deducted: approved, it is Dr 6100 Salaries; what is to be paid is Cr 2100 Salaries payable, and the advances taken back Cr 1300.” and “Gross {gross}.”

controls.label: Adjust…
controls.does: On a draft's line: Added, What it is for (e.g. a bonus for Eid), Deducted, What it is for (e.g. absent on the 12th), Advance taken back (empty: all owed, as far as the pay goes); “Save” and “Cancel”.
controls.rules: Amounts of zero or more. A note is needed for any addition or deduction. Deductions no more than earned. Take back no more than owed nor more than the pay.

controls.label: Pay…

controls.after: Journal: Dr 2100 Salaries payable, Cr 1000 / 1005 / 1020 / 3000. From the till, the drawer's expected cash goes down. When everyone is paid in full the payroll becomes Paid.

messages.when: A save was sent again with its first key but different values (for example, the form was changed while it was retrying).
messages.do: Reload the page, check whether the first save went through, then do it again if needed.

messages.text: This was sent by someone else
messages.when: Rare: the same save key was already used by another person's login.
messages.do: Reload the page and do it again.

messages.text: You do not have permission to do this (needs {1})
messages.when: Your roles do not hold the permission named (here usually discount.approve). The database checks every save again, even if a button was shown.
messages.do: Ask the owner to change your roles on Settings → People and roles, or ask someone who may do it.

messages.text: Finish signing in: type the code from your authenticator app
messages.when: Two-step sign-in is on for you and this session has not taken the second step.
messages.do: Reload the page: you are taken to the code step. Type the six digits from your authenticator app.

messages.text: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
messages.when: The sign-in expired or was ended on this device.
messages.do: Sign in again; what you typed may need typing again.

messages.text: The database did not answer, so this may have been saved. Check before trying again.
messages.when: The connection to the database failed during a save that has no automatic retry.
messages.do: Reload the page and look whether the change is there before doing it again.

messages.text: The database is missing an update this screen needs (a migration has not been applied yet).
messages.when: The café's database has not had the update that this part of the screen uses.
messages.do: Tell whoever looks after the system; nothing was saved.

what_if.case: Someone may know my password
what_if.do: Change password here, and turn on two-step sign-in.

what_if.case: I lost the phone with the authenticator app
what_if.do: This screen cannot help without the code: ask whoever runs the system to remove the second step, then turn it on again with the new phone.

what_if.case: I want the app in Kurdish
what_if.do: Choose کوردی in the Language list at the top.
